summary: Milestone 2026.09.672 completed 9 experiments, all compute-bound, totaling 58.3 wall-time minutes (average 6 minutes per experiment) with timing reconstructed via disk-mtime fallback. Execution time was heavily concentrated in the top three compute-bound experiments—'Seal unexposed natural source families and isolate evaluation labels' at 19.93 minutes, 'Qualify complete sentence windows and a finite latent-evidence energy' at 16.57 minutes, and 'Qualify commits, rejection and complete-static controls for the advisory bank' at 11.56 minutes—accounting for 48.06 of 58.3 total wall-time minutes (82.4%). GPU idle on compute-bound tasks was false, and intra-task phase durations remained unmeasured.
bottlenecks_identified: The slowest experiment ('Seal unexposed natural source families and isolate evaluation labels') required 19.93 minutes, consuming 34.2% of the 58.3 total milestone wall-time minutes alone, but the lack of sub-phase profiling prevents isolating time spent on model inference versus evaluation label isolation and data serialization.

The top three slowest compute-bound experiments ('Seal unexposed natural source families and isolate evaluation labels' at 19.93 minutes, 'Qualify complete sentence windows and a finite latent-evidence energy' at 16.57 minutes, and 'Qualify commits, rejection and complete-static controls for the advisory bank' at 11.56 minutes) accounted for 48.06 of 58.3 total minutes (82.4%), representing extreme execution concentration without intra-task stage breakdown.

The post-run GPU monitor report captures an idle state (GPU 0 at 5MB, 0% util; GPU 1 at 4MB, 0% util) at milestone completion, but because gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is false, this reflects post-run quiescence rather than an active-task bottleneck; continuous in-run GPU telemetry across active task windows was absent.
No experiment records indicate concurrent execution of two or more models in parallel, so DualGPURunner dispatch was not applicable to the single-model tasks executed this milestone.

Capture continuous active-window GPU utilization and VRAM metrics during compute-bound executions to evaluate accelerator efficiency throughout task runs.
Persist model concurrency and runner dispatch metadata in experiment receipts to formally verify DualGPURunner applicability on multi-model workloads.
Emit synchronous, structured start and finish timestamps directly to experiment execution receipts to avoid falling back to filesystem disk-mtime reconstruction.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument sub-phase duration profiling inside source family sealing and sentence window energy evaluation routines to isolate model inference latency from evaluation overhead.
Deploy continuous in-task GPU utilization monitoring during compute-bound runs to capture active-window accelerator throughput.

meta_reflection: Milestone 2026.09.672 executed 9 compute-bound tasks across 58.3 wall-time minutes, with 82.4% of total runtime concentrated in the top three experiments led by source family sealing at 19.93 minutes and sentence window qualification at 16.57 minutes. While the post-run GPU monitor snapshot recorded both RTX 3090 GPUs idle (5MB/4MB allocated, 0% utilization), gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is false and active-window accelerator efficiency was not continuously logged, with no multi-model tasks present to engage DualGPURunner. Implementing fine-grained sub-phase timing and continuous accelerator telemetry represents the most effective operational path to isolating bottlenecks in upcoming compute-heavy milestones.
